title: Per-task run_terminal via human grant replace
description:
**Phase 1.** Parent epic `chatticus-598be4`. Ties `chatticus-e11c17` (`run_terminal` tool) to Shape 1: per-task human grant.

`run_terminal` must **not** enter `household_conversation_grant()`. A customer bot gets a shell only when a human replaces the turn grant with one that includes `run_terminal` (and file_scopes for cwd).

Depends on `chatticus-be3997` (and `chatticus-753bd8` if that is how the human submits). Live `e11c17` host proof may still be blocked on `HOST_NOT_RUNNING`; this card is the **customer authority path**, not another kernel deviation.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Per-task run_terminal via human grant replace
  As an enabled organization member
  I want to authorize a shell for one turn by replacing its grant
  So a default conversation bot still cannot run_terminal

  Scenario: Conversation preset still denies run_terminal
    Given a human-started turn with the household conversation grant
    When the bot attempts run_terminal
    Then the turn journal records a denied run_terminal tool result

  Scenario: A replaced grant that includes run_terminal is allowed by policy
    Given a human-started turn with the household conversation grant
    When an enabled member replaces the active turn grant with:
      | field          | value                         |
      | tools          | read_workspace, run_terminal  |
      | origins        |                               |
      | recipients     |                               |
      | file_scopes    | /workspace                    |
      | egress_classes | approved_origin_fetch         |
    And the bot attempts run_terminal under /workspace
    Then the turn is not denied for lack of run_terminal on the grant
```

## Done when

Gherkin shows a human-replaced turn can `run_terminal` and a conversation-preset turn cannot. Do not live-poll a stopped host to rediscover `HOST_NOT_RUNNING`.
